MOVES_FREE's own code does `bl 0x80003100` at 0x8012E9F0 (memset of the entry's buffer, whenever the entry is not in use by the current player's object), and 0x80003100 is the intercept hle_msl_memset (run logs: "[hle] native memcpy 0x800031EC memset 0x80003100"), a whole replacement: the nested dispatch leaves g_hle_passthrough = false. p2_moves_load then fails AFTER that loop (8091 no file, 8109 "no part %d in %s" / part too big for the slot, 8116 MOVES_READY fails; MOVES_READY and MOVES_SETS reach no intercept, so nothing puts the flag back) and returns false; line 8243-8244 `if (!p2_moves_load(...)) return;` returns with pass-through meant on but the flag off.

Call site 0x80132318 does `or r31, r3, r3` and hands that back as the answer, so non-zero reads as ready; the game's 0x80132970 (which answers 0/1 in r29 and applies the part with 0x80133310) does not run. g_p2_moves[k] was already cleared at 8085; the object's +644/+648/+652 still name its other slot, so it keeps playing the part it had.

verdicts.risk_of_fix: With the flag put back, the game's own 0x80132970 runs for player 2's (or another playable's) object on every failed load, not only when nothing was freed. It writes that object and part into the game's moves record (0x80582008 / 0x8058200C) and can take or let go one of the game's two slots (0x801327B4), which are player 1's: the comment at 8177-8180 says that is what twisted Paul. This is already what happens today whenever no old part was freed, so the fix makes the path consistent rather than adding a new behaviour, but it is not obviously the better answer. In the one logged case the part number was garbage (29572504), and the game's function would be handed that. If passing through is not wanted here, the alternative is a handled answer of 0 (`g_hle_passthrough = false; hle_set_u32(cpu, 0u);`), which makes the caller ask again each frame and repeats the unthrottled stderr line at 8110. verdicts.risk_of_fix: Low. Nothing on this path works today because the original is skipped: in the everyday case the flag is already true and the game's function already runs with the r4 that moves_part chose, so the fix only makes the rare failed-serve case behave the same. The weapon slot k that the failed serve wrote over is the one player 1 is not playing from (9644-9645) and g_p2_moves[k] is cleared (8085 / 9659), so the game's function running afterwards reads nothing stale from it.
